alex: running a quick nsys sweep on the INT8+FP8 combo to hunt a latency regression after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. attaching observations below.

maya: nice, paste the exact command you used?

alex: `nsys profile --output deq-lockstep --trace=cuda,cudnn,kernels -t 30 --sample=none ./load_test --model gpt-small --batch 8 --max-tokens 512`

sam: initial note: seen a 10-18% p99 bump on the canary traffic after the selector started preferring int8-deq kernels for seq<=128.

alex: trace shows a recurring pattern where decoder kernels finish but the dequant/cast kernels execute serially across threads, not overlapped with prefix KV streaming. timeline snippet: 
```
kernel: decoder_block_N  0.0 - 9.1ms
kernel: int8_dequant     9.2 - 9.7ms  <-- serialized against other streams
kernel: kv_prefetch      9.8 - 11.0ms <-- waits on hostcopy
kernel: decoder_block_N+1 11.1 - 20.3ms
```

maya: that looks like stream synchronization or implicit device->host copy. did you see host->device memcpys around kv_prefetch?

alex: yes. nvtx regions show `hostcopy_kv_write` right before `kv_prefetch`. nvprof stacks point to `cudaMemcpyAsync` on stream 0.

perf-bot: automated note: sampling shows kernel occupancy drop during dequant phases; avg SM utilization fell from 72% -> 43% in those slices.

sam: hypothesis: our dequant implementation uses a synchronous CUDA stream or blocks default stream, causing cross-stream serialisation. Also the kernel selector may choose a smaller grid for int8 that doesn't saturate SMs — more launches in sequence -> more kernel launch overhead.

maya: can we try two quick experiments? 1) force dequant on separate non-blocking stream and prewarm kernel grid size to match FP8 launch config. 2) run only decoder with kv cache warm to exclude hostcopy.

alex: running exp1 now. patch: bind dequant to stream `deq_s` and do `cudaMemcpyAsync` with that stream for dequant outputs. also added `--force-grid 256`.

alex: results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~6%, p99 improved ~12%. timeline shows dequant overlapped with decoder+kv prefetch more often.

sam: promising. did accuracy change with the forced grid? any bit flips?

alex: no measurable logprob drift on sanity prompts; still running a longer eval.

maya: exp2 (no hostcopy) results?

alex: with cache warmed and hostcopy disabled, p99 drops back to baseline. conclusion: hostcopy + default stream behavior is the main culprit; dequant launches were aligning with hostcopy on stream0 and forcing serialization.

perf-bot: note: nvlink transfer rate during hostcopy spikes correlated with CPU-side stalls; system counters show PCIe queue depth hitting max for short bursts.

sam: two follow-ups: 1) update kernel selector to prefer dequant kernels compiled for non-default-stream (i.e., stream-aware launches) when kv_prefetch exists. 2) add a batching heuristic that attempts to schedule dequant work earlier to increase overlap.

maya: also check quantization path for FP8 fast path — it had lower launch overhead but slightly higher float ops; might be preferable for small seq lengths. Need perf/accuracy tradeoff measurement.

alex: I've got nsys profiles saved: `deq-lockstep.qdrep` and short perfetto slices uploaded to the perf artifacts bucket: https://perf.redwood/dev/deq-lockstep/1775552468 (internal).

tess: quick ops question — will changing streams break any current rollback or tracing hooks? our tracing assumes stream 0 for some nvtx spans.

sam: good catch. we'll need to emit NVTX in the new stream and map it in the agent so traces still correlate. also add a sentinel event on hostcopy boundary.

maya: for the kernel selector patch, propose a conservative rollout: config flag `enable_deq_streaming` off by default for hosted, enable for Dedicated experiments. Canary 5% then 25%.

alex: I'll open a PR with the changes + nsys traces and a short reproducer script. PR will include benchmark harness and a short accuracy eval.

sam: add a regression test to CI that runs the small harness with warmed kv cache and compares p99 against baseline within 5%.

alex: will do. final note: INT8 still wins costwise, but for seq<=64 FP8 might actually be overall faster due to fewer dequant sync points. we should feed this into the model routing policy too.

maya: thanks — great sleuthing. :tada:

perf-bot: automated summary: root cause -> dequant launch/hostcopy serialization on default stream; mitigations -> stream-aware dequant launches, pinned grid sizes for small seq, KV hostcopy mapping to avoid blocking.

alex: leaving the traces and short howto in the PR, ping me if you want raw qdrep.

sam: ack, will review.
